newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler international sales up 19.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler international sales up 19.4 pct.

text.p: Chrysler International, a unit of Chrysler Corp, said Wednesday that retail sales of vehicles outside North America in calendar 1996 rose 19.4 percent over record results a year earlier.
Chrysler said calendar 1996 sales rose to 222,035 vehicles from the previous record of 185,934 set in 1995.

"We are seeing growth in each of our global regions, paced by the continued popularity of our Jeep vehicles and our minivans," said Francois Castaing, executive vice president of Chrysler's international and powertrain operations.
"In fact, Jeep products -- Grand Cherokee, Cherokee and Wrangler -- in both left- and right-hand-drive configurations, account for almost half of our international sales," he said in a statement.

Sales of Chrysler minivans outside North America totaled 52,530 in 1996, up 21 percent over 1995. With the introduction of right-hand-drive minivans over the next several months, these vehicles should continue to experience significant growth in 1997, he said.
Growth of in sales of passenger cars internationally were led by the Neon with over 29,000 units, up 22 percent over last year and the Stratus, with over 15,000, up 59 percent over last year.
Europe continues to be the largest regional market for Chrysler, with 102,139 units in 1996, followed by Asia/Pacific (78,121), Latin America (22,515) and Middle East/Africa (19,260).
Latin America and the Middle East/Africa regions experienced the largest percentage increase, 11 percent and 36 percent, respectively.
Chrysler International operates in over 140 countries outside the United States, Canada and Mexico.
